name: People's Multiparty Democracy
summary: People's Multiparty Democracy is the programme the Communist Party of Nepal (Marxist-Leninist) adopted in 1993 under Madan Bhandari. It keeps Marxism-Leninism and the goal of socialism but drops one-party rule and proletarian dictatorship, committing the party to competitive elections, multi-party competition, separation of powers and human rights. It sets a mixed economy with compensated land reform and foreign capital as the route to socialism in a semi-feudal, semi-colonial Nepal.
scope: Madan Bhandari's 1993 programme 'People's Multiparty Democracy: A Program of Nepali Revolution' as adopted by the CPN (Unified Marxist-Leninist) and described in scholarly summaries of its fourteen features. It excludes later party practice and the compromise 'People's Democracy' line of the 2009 Maoist merger. The programme text itself was not available to me; the sources summarise and quote it.

sources.title: People's Multiparty Democracy: Marxist Foundation of Democracy and Human Rights
sources.author: S. Pyakurel, State, Society and Development: PMPD Perspectives 4(1) (2026)
sources.usedFor: Abstract only: PMPD treats democracy and human rights as integral to the socialist project.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The party supports a welfare system guaranteeing social security and social justice for all citizens, which suggests state-guaranteed health care, though no source mentions health specifically.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Inferred from the programme's identification of workers as the main and decisive class for change and its aim of ending exploitation; wage policy is not discussed.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The programme defends a mixed economy and foreign capital but treats profit-seeking as exploitative and aims at socialism, so adherents would doubt markets beat governments; not stated directly.

public-ownership.rationale: The programme calls for building economic and social infrastructure for the transition to socialism and for social state institutions within a mixed economy, implying public ownership of major sectors.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Inferred from its egalitarian goals and opposition to unlimited wealth accumulation; taxation policy is not in the sources I opened.

unions-good.rationale: Workers and farmers are named as the main and decisive forces of transformation, and a party built on them would back organised labour.

property-fundamental.rationale: The programme abolishes feudal land ownership by compensated land reform and treats ownership of resources as the root of inequality, so property is not an inviolable right.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Inferred from hostility to comprador and foreign monopoly capital and a state that steers development in the national interest; regulation is not discussed.

cut-welfare.rationale: The party supports a welfare system guaranteeing social security, so cutting welfare as harmful dependency runs against its stated line.

worker-ownership.rationale: Socialism is the stated goal and collective economic relations are to be encouraged, but the programme does not specify worker-owned firms, so this is inferred.

surveillance-ok.rationale: The programme says fundamental rights must not be confiscated and no one may be treated arbitrarily; surveillance for security is not addressed, so this is inferred.

legalize-drugs.rationale: The sources are silent on drugs; a conservative-leaning Nepali communist party would likely not back legalization.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Bhandari insists on very broad freedom of expression, yet a party committed to equality and ethnic plurality could accept some limits, so adherents are plausibly split.

strong-leader.rationale: The programme rejects centralisation at personal and organisational level and requires separation of powers, so a leader bypassing gridlock contradicts it.

state-harmful.rationale: PMPD treats the state as a necessary instrument whose class character must be changed, and builds a people's state rather than abolishing it.

limit-guns.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the programme's emphasis on peaceful politics and rule of law.

empower-police-military.rationale: The programme warns against arbitrary state power and an armed party; no source discusses police budgets, so this is inferred.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: The sources are silent and communist parties in Nepal are not clearly aligned either way.

decide-locally.rationale: The party lists federalism among its principles and stresses Nepal's diversity, which points to some devolution; not stated for this question.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred from the human-rights emphasis and rule of law; penal policy is not discussed.

traditional-family.rationale: PMPD stresses ending discrimination and women's proportional representation, so it is unlikely to treat traditional family structures as the foundation; inferred.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; inferred from the party's human-rights and equality commitments.

abortion-legal.rationale: The sources say nothing on abortion; support is inferred from the programme's commitments to women's equality and human rights, so confidence is low.

more-religion-public.rationale: The programme is materialist and treats rulers' supernatural claims as overcome, so a larger public religious role is unlikely to be favoured; inferred.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: PMPD aims to end all discrimination in a plural, multi-ethnic Nepal; policies for historical injustice are inferred rather than stated.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The sources never address gender theory, and adherents are not clearly split or aligned.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The party is described as left-wing nationalist and the programme counts nationalist and patriotic classes as allies, though it also values plurality.

gradual-change.rationale: The programme pursues a peaceful parliamentary revolution under constitutional supremacy, which favours institutional, step-by-step change.

reduce-immigration.rationale: The sources do not address immigration, and nothing in the programme points either way.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The programme's foreign policy rests on Panchsheel, which stresses sovereignty and non-interference; strengthening international bodies is inferred to be disfavoured.

free-trade.rationale: The programme welcomes foreign capital but seeks a self-reliant national economy and opposes foreign monopoly capital, so free trade benefiting everyone is doubted; inferred.

nation-first.rationale: Left-wing nationalism and an independent, self-reliant economy point to putting national interest first, though the sources do not state it for this question.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: The programme bases foreign policy on Panchsheel, whose principles include non-interference in others' affairs.

open-borders.rationale: Not addressed; the national-independence emphasis makes open borders an unlikely goal.

limit-growth.rationale: The programme aims at developing productive forces and a self-reliant economy, so limiting growth is unlikely; inferred.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Climate is not mentioned; inferred from the state-led development and people's-welfare orientation.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The programme welcomes technology and foreign technology but also says technology aggravates inequality, so it is split.

expand-nuclear.rationale: None of the sources I opened mention nuclear power, and nothing in PMPD's principles favours or opposes it, so a neutral answer is the honest one.

revolution-justified.rationale: Violent struggle is justified if the ruling party violently suppresses peaceful, legal struggle, although the present path is peaceful.

experts-over-public.rationale: The programme puts the people above party, state and any body, so rule by experts is disfavoured; inferred.

central-planning.rationale: The programme endorses a mixed economy and multi-party competition rather than a fully planned economy.

socialized-markets.rationale: Inferred from the mixed-economy model and goal of social institutions; not stated for market socialism specifically.

land-value-tax.rationale: Land taxation is not discussed; the programme addresses land through compensated reform.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from the programme's aim of ending inequality that stems from ownership and its hostility to unlimited wealth accumulation; inheritance tax is never mentioned.

basic-income.rationale: The party backs welfare and social security, but an unconditional basic income is not discussed.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Inferred from the aim of an independent self-reliant national industrial economy and hostility to comprador capital.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Inferred from the state's role in building infrastructure for the transition to socialism and in developing national capital.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Land reform lets middle and rich peasants keep land and national capitalists are allies, yet socialism opposes private concentration, so no clear stance.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Communism is the long-run goal, but the programme is a transitional mixed-economy plan, so abolishing money and wages is not on the agenda.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Not discussed; a state-guided mixed economy would not hand money to the market.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Not discussed; the multiparty, pluralist framework does not point to state-recognised corporatist bodies.

one-party-rule.rationale: The programme states that recognising a one-party system or dictatorship is wrong and that no class or party may be barred from competing.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The party backed a constitutional monarchy only early on, later called for and helped establish a federal democratic republic, and describes the monarchy as an end of supernatural rule.

democracy-best.rationale: The programme treats people's supremacy and competitive elections as central, even requiring a victorious communist party to place the people highest and face repeat approval.

direct-votes.rationale: Referendums are named among the ways people assert themselves, but the programme centres on representative multi-party competition.

workers-councils.rationale: The programme rests on parliamentary multi-party competition under a constitution, not on councils as the basis of power.

right-to-secede.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; the party lists federalism among its principles, which implies autonomy within one state rather than a right to leave.

natural-rulers.rationale: People are declared the masters of the country and leaders are chosen through competition and election, excluding any natural right to rule.

political-violence-never.rationale: The programme says violence is not always to be met with peace and that armed resistance is justified against violent suppression of peaceful struggle.

war-builds-character.rationale: Not addressed; contradicts the programme's peaceful-coexistence foreign policy and people's welfare focus.

separate-church-state.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the materialist outlook and the programme's rejection of supernatural sources of authority.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Inferred from the programme's materialism and its rule of law grounded in the constitution of the sovereign people.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Inferred: the programme wants a rule of law enforced by an authorised legal body and a state serving the people.

military-superiority.rationale: Panchsheel foreign policy favours peaceful coexistence; military superiority is not mentioned.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Bhandari justified multi-party rule by Nepal being culturally, ethnically and linguistically plural, rejecting one-group nationhood.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The programme holds that class struggle drives social change and that classes arise from ownership of resources, as in Marxism-Leninism.

equal-outcomes.rationale: The programme aims at a just, egalitarian society that ends discrimination and exploitation, beyond equal opportunity.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; the programme's plural-society commitment does not settle this question.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Anti-imperialism is part of the line, but no source mentions reparations, so adherents' view cannot be stated and is left neutral.

civilizational-union.rationale: Not addressed; the programme's national-independence and Panchsheel orientation weigh against.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The programme treats profit seeking as the root of exploitation and stresses collective welfare; inferred.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Bhandari said fundamental rights must not be confiscated even after revolution, and rights must not be controlled by party or state.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Nature and diversity are praised in the programme's philosophy, but its value is not discussed.

limit-population.rationale: Not discussed; the programme says ownership, not nature or population, is the root of inequality.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The programme seeks to build industry and a self-reliant industrial economy; inferred.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Foreign technology is welcomed and productive forces are to be developed, though disruption of institutions is not endorsed.

human-enhancement.rationale: Human enhancement is outside anything the sources discuss; no principle of PMPD bears on it, so it is neutral.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Inferred from the stress on people's decisive role and accountability of leaders.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Digital privacy is not discussed; the programme's rule-of-law and anti-arbitrary-power stance gives no clear direction, so it is neutral.

restore-past-order.rationale: The programme aims to end the semi-feudal, semi-colonial order and build a new society.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Bhandari's slogan that principles are for life, not life for principles, and that Marxism is not dogma supports judging by results.

direct-action.rationale: The programme prioritises elections and parliament while allowing non-parliamentary actions in tactics, so direct action is not preferred.

means-match-ends.rationale: The programme says the goal is primary and means secondary and adaptable, though it embraces democratic means.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Inconsistent with the programme's aim of developing production and technology.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Not addressed; the programme concerns near-term socialism, not abolishing the division of labour.

distribute-by-need.rationale: The programme places communism, reached through socialism, as the goal of the struggle against exploitation.

production-for-use.rationale: Inferred from criticism of capitalist profit seeking and the socialist goal.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The programme says capitalists' central aim of profit cannot be achieved without exploiting the workforce, though national capitalists are accepted allies.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: PMPD replaces proletarian dictatorship with a people's democratic state, rejecting one-party dictatorship and holding that no class may be prohibited.

collective-farming.rationale: The land reform compensates landlords and lets rich and middle peasants keep and use their land, not collectivise it.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: The programme condemns imperialism and foreign monopoly capitalism but does not discuss great-power wars.

taxation-theft.rationale: A party backing a welfare system financed by the state rejects this libertarian claim; inferred.

harm-principle.rationale: Bhandari defended broad freedoms of opinion and expression, though the programme also allows controlling anti-progressive elements.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Not stated; the programme stresses people and class as collective subjects as well as individual rights.

conscription.rationale: Not discussed; the programme says the party should not be military and people's rights should be protected.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The programme stresses the vote and people's supremacy as the main check on power.

state-as-business.rationale: Inferred from its welfare-state and public-interest conception of the state.

positive-liberty.rationale: PMPD treats democracy and human rights as part of a project of socio-economic transformation, implying freedom needs material conditions.

media-academia-power.rationale: The programme locates power in classes and state structures, not in media and universities.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Inferred from the programme's materialist view that discrimination stems from ownership relations.

organic-representation.rationale: The programme requires multi-party competition and periodic elections as its essence, not corporate or family representation.

total-state.rationale: The programme requires separation of powers, a state-party boundary and a pluralist open society.

national-rebirth.rationale: Not discussed; the programme prefers concrete class analysis over a decadence narrative.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Foreign policy is based on Panchsheel, which includes respect for territorial integrity and non-aggression.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The programme targets feudal forms of rule and puts constitution and law above any person.

bound-labor.rationale: The programme's central economic aim is to end the semi-feudal order and its land relations, so bound labour owed to a lord is the opposite of its goal.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Not discussed; Marxism has ideology-critique elements but the programme stresses scientific method.

universal-morality.rationale: Not discussed; Marxist class analysis tends to doubt universal morals, though human rights are universal in PMPD.

single-common-good.rationale: The programme sees society as made of classes with different interests, competing through parties.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The sources never discuss Israel or Zionism, and a Nepali communist party with Panchsheel-based foreign policy has no stated line, so it is left neutral.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Diaspora citizenship is not covered in any source I opened and no principle of PMPD settles it.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language revival is not discussed; Bhandari emphasised linguistic plurality, but that does not decide whether a fallen-out-of-use language should be revived.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Inferred from the programme's call to democratise party, society and state and its socialist aim; firm governance is not specified.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education policy is not discussed beyond the aim of social infrastructure; inferred opposition to market-style provision from the state-led, socialist-leaning orientation.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal policy is not discussed; inferred from a state expected to drive development and welfare rather than follow orthodox budget limits.

economic-freedom.rationale: The programme presents political freedoms as grounded in people's supremacy, not market freedom.

rule-by-example.rationale: The programme demands rule of law, constitutional supremacy and no arbitrary decisions by anyone in power.

national-self-determination.rationale: Left-wing nationalism and anti-imperialism imply support; not directly stated.

force-without-un.rationale: Panchsheel-based foreign policy stresses sovereignty and peaceful relations, so unilateral force abroad is inferred to be disfavoured; the UN is not discussed.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Dialectical materialism and scientific socialism frame the programme, though emotion and faith are not discussed.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: The welfare system is for all citizens; the sources say nothing about immigrants.

work-for-welfare.rationale: A welfare system guaranteeing social security suggests no work test; inferred.

class-collaboration.rationale: The programme says revolution follows class struggle, not class coordination, though it allies with national capitalists.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the programme's aim of developing the country materially and spiritually, which does not suggest discarding institutions.

dominated-front.rationale: Panchsheel foreign policy and anti-imperialism pull in different directions.

workers-nation.rationale: The programme seeks solidarity with the world communist movement but builds an alliance of patriotic classes nationally.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The programme calls for women's proportional representation; distinct legal roles are inferred to be rejected.

ban-interest.rationale: Not discussed; the programme accepts a mixed economy with foreign and national capital.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Contrary to its commitments to human rights, pluralism and ending discrimination.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The programme says state power arose with classes and that the key question is which class's interests it serves, calling the old state a tool of the capitalist class.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy policy is not covered in the sources and PMPD's principles do not point either way.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Bhandari prized cultural plurality, so forced assimilation is unlikely; inferred.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy theory with no place in the programme, whose analysis of power is class-based (feudal, comprador and foreign monopoly capital), so inferred rejection.

proportional-representation.rationale: The programme supports free, fair competitive elections; proportional allocation is not stated.

national-mission.rationale: Spreading one's government to other peoples contradicts Panchsheel non-interference, the programme's stated foreign-policy basis.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Its commitment to women's proportional representation suggests acceptance of structural disadvantage; inferred.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The programme blames crony bureaucratic bourgeoisie and comprador classes for controlling the state.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenic discouragement of births contradicts the programme's commitments to human rights and ending discrimination; inferred rather than discussed.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Inferred from rule of law, protection of human rights and the ban on arbitrary decisions by those in power; past abuses are not specifically discussed.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The party backs a welfare state and the programme gives the state a development role.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Contradicts the programme's commitments to ending discrimination and to an open, plural society; inferred.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The programme aims to end all discrimination and guarantee human rights to everyone.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Bhandari programmed a Nepal-specific revolution applying Marxism creatively; he does not make socialism depend on revolutions elsewhere.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: The sources never address settler states, so no position can be stated, and anti-imperialism does not settle individual cases.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Equal rights under one constitution suggest support; family law is not discussed.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Freedom of opinion is stressed, yet Nepali politics, including the UML, is split on conversion limits.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Cow slaughter is not discussed in the sources; Nepali political opinion, including adherents, is mixed on it.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Inferred from the materialist outlook and the rejection of supernatural authority.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: The programme warns against one-party state power and emphasises democratisation of the state.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The programme holds that people are the source of state power and that leaders must be periodically approved by the people, even after a revolution.

trade-surplus.rationale: Trade balance policy is not mentioned; PMPD's self-reliance and openness to foreign capital pull in different directions.

population-transfer.rationale: Pressuring a minority to leave contradicts the programme's human-rights and anti-discrimination commitments; inferred.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The programme condemns initiating violence against the people but allows force against violent suppression.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: PMPD stresses competition within politics but sees class struggle, not peoples' competition, as driving history.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The programme says no class should be prohibited from the state and that all parties may compete.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Its demand that no person in power may decide arbitrarily fits this view; inferred.

separated-powers.rationale: The programme lists separation of powers as a core feature; no single body should hold executive, legislative and judicial powers.

vanguard-party.rationale: The programme keeps the party as a Marxist-Leninist leader of class movements with democratic centralism, though democratised and not a state party.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The programme names workers and poor and middle farmers as the main classes for change and aims at a just, egalitarian society.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Housing policy is not discussed; inferred disfavour from the socialist tilt towards public provision, with low confidence.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Labour law is not discussed; a party founded on workers and farmers as the decisive classes is inferred to oppose such limits.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The programme says the root of inequality is the ownership of resources, not population.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Bhandari argued a one-party system suits no country as plural as Nepal and treated cultural, ethnic and linguistic diversity as natural and enriching.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Leaders should be chosen through struggle, competition and periodic elections.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Bhandari said fundamental rights must not be confiscated even after revolution.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price policy is not discussed; inferred from a state expected to serve the people's welfare in a mixed economy.

party-controls-media.rationale: Bhandari said everyone must be able to criticise government and party and to seek and impart information through any media.

party-commands-army.rationale: The programme says the party should not be a military or state party and requires a clear demarcation between state and ruling party.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Citizenship rules are not discussed in the sources I opened.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Inferred from the communist tradition and anti-privilege stance; pay for legislators is not addressed.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: The programme upholds democratic centralism and self-conscious discipline within the party.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Panchsheel and the emphasis on national independence suggest wariness of pooling sovereignty, though supranational unions are never discussed.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The party works in a parliamentary system and the programme requires separation of powers, so a head of state commanding forces and picking ministers is disfavoured.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is a religious matter with no connection to the programme's content, so it has no stated position.

clerical-rule.rationale: The programme makes the people the source of state power and rejects supernatural sources of authority, so rule by senior clerics is excluded.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: A Leninist line, but the programme's patriotism and focus on national independence leave it unclear.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Bhandari insisted on an open society with freedom to speak, seek and impart ideas through any media, so moral censorship of art runs against it.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Periodic elections and competition for leadership imply turnover; term limits are not discussed, so this is inferred.

recall-officials.rationale: The programme says leaders must be periodically approved by the people; recall within a term is not mentioned.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Panchsheel-based foreign policy suggests non-alignment and ending military blocs; inferred rather than stated.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Housing tenure is not discussed; abolishing renting would conflict with a mixed economy.

people-in-arms.rationale: The programme says party should not be military; armed citizenry not discussed.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Programme seeks industrialisation and moving workforce into industry and commerce.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, and nothing in PMPD's principles decides this.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Not discussed; the programme names professionals among the classes favouring change, which weighs mildly against this view.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Bhandari's emphasis on cultural and ethnic plurality suggests equality of cultures.

death-penalty.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the programme's human-rights emphasis.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Inferred from the scientific, materialist outlook and the commitment to women's equality; school curricula are not discussed.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Dialectical materialism is the philosophical basis of PMPD, so teaching creationism alongside evolution is inferred to be rejected.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Not discussed in any source; no principle of PMPD settles it.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Not discussed; citizenship rules are not addressed in the sources.

minority-language-support.rationale: Bhandari invoked Nepal's linguistic and ethnic diversity as the basis for pluralism.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Not discussed; freedom of opinion is stressed but exemptions from general law are not.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Bhandari called for a pluralistic open society in which everyone can think and speak freely.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Anti-imperialism suggests sympathy for cancelling poor countries' debts, but debt is not discussed, so low confidence.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The programme says the semi-feudal, semi-colonial economic base must be ended to establish independence and a self-reliant economy.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The party has campaigned for a Constituent Assembly since the 1950s and its 2006 movement led to one.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The programme says fundamental rights should not be confiscated even after revolution, and opposes autocratic one-party authority.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Inferred from solidarity with other countries' movements and anti-imperialism; aid duties are not discussed.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Panchsheel-based peaceful foreign policy and Nepal's small-state position make an own nuclear deterrent unlikely to be favoured; inferred.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Method of electing a head of state is not covered in the sources.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Monetary policy is not discussed; inferred disfavour for insulating policy from elected governments, given a state-led development aim.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territorial disputes are not covered in the sources; no position follows from PMPD principles.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: The programme redefines property relations to serve people's needs and abolishes feudal landholding.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The sources say Soviet failure was one-party misuse of state power, but do not call it state capitalism.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the programme's people-first, welfare-oriented view of the state.

collective-defense.rationale: Panchsheel and non-alignment suggest wariness of mutual-defence blocs; alliances are not discussed.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Inferred from Panchsheel's respect for sovereignty and territorial integrity.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Not discussed; a materialist outlook points one way but the sources give no policy on religious institutions.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The party backed a republic; a ceremonial, non-partisan head of state is inferred from its separation-of-powers stance.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Not discussed; adherents could favour national unity or peaceful settlement, so no clear position.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Special autonomy arrangements are not discussed; the party lists federalism but gives no view on distinct economic systems.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The paper says people ended belief in kings and supernatural beings as sources of state power.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Tax policy is not discussed; a flat tax contradicts the programme's egalitarian aims, so inferred opposition.

character-from-environment.rationale: Inferred from the materialist view that social conditions shape consciousness.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The programme says no class, person, institution or party can be above the constitution.

space-expansion.rationale: Space policy appears nowhere in the sources I opened, and no PMPD principle bears on it, so the answer is neutral.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical mixed-constitution theory is not addressed; PMPD's separation of powers and elections do not map onto it.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family courts are not discussed in any source I opened.

land-redistribution.rationale: Revolutionary land reform with compensation to landlords gives land to those who farm it.

refugee-return.rationale: Inferred from the programme's human-rights commitments; no source discusses refugees.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Contradicts the freedom of opinion Bhandari defended as a right not to be confiscated even after a revolution.

women-must-cover.rationale: Contradicts the programme's commitments to women's equality and fundamental freedoms; inferred.

common-currency.rationale: Monetary union is not discussed; Nepali communist sources give no line, and the programme's national-independence emphasis does not settle it.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Inferred disfavour from national independence and Panchsheel respect for existing sovereign states.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Not discussed; Bhandari valued ethnic and linguistic plurality, but cultural autonomy as a policy is not stated.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Inferred from commitment to equal rights and pluralism within each country.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Production relations and productive forces drive revolution in the programme.

ban-cartels.rationale: Inferred from the programme's hostility to monopoly capital; competition law is not discussed.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bank and firm rescues are not discussed; PMPD's mixed economy and state role give no clear direction, so it is neutral.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: The programme says no class, person or party can be above the constitution, so courts may constrain majorities.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: The programme says the party should achieve proportional representation of women.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: The programme invites foreign capital and technology and favours coexistence, so a closed bloc is rejected.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Inferred from the worker-friendly orientation; trade agreements are not discussed.

moral-incentives.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; no stated view on incentives versus social duty.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The programme says revolution is not to be rushed by leaders' haste and rejects adventurism; Jhapa campaign failure prompted reform.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The party took part in ending the monarchy and targets semi-feudal relations, so hereditary titles and privileges are opposed.

history-own-civilization.rationale: School history is not discussed in any source.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Anti-imperialism and the target of foreign monopoly capital and imperialism make rule by supposedly advanced societies unacceptable.

patriotic-education.rationale: The party is described as left-wing nationalist and counts patriotic classes as allies, so patriotic schooling is inferred; low confidence.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Not discussed; the programme's aim of ending discrimination suggests it would not abolish remedial preferences.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary design is not discussed in any source.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Not discussed; Panchsheel respect for sovereignty weighs against pursuing influence over former dominions.

delink-world-market.rationale: The programme invites foreign capital and technology under national law, so delinking is rejected.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Not discussed; the programme's class analysis is national, not about rich-world workers.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Constitutional supremacy and human-rights protection are core features, which favours an entrenched rights document.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Inferred from anti-imperialism; no source discusses colonial-era treaties.

elective-rulers.rationale: Leaders and parties get their mandate through periodic elections on universal adult franchise.

minority-veto.rationale: The programme sets majority government with minority opposition, not minority consent as a condition of binding decisions.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The programme holds that violent struggle becomes justified if rulers violently suppress legal, peaceful struggle and subvert the constitution.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The party works within a parliamentary system where governments are formed through competitive elections, though the constitution is above parliament.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal welfare is not discussed in any source.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal use is not discussed in any source.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: The programme prefers structural change over charity of the privileged, as it locates inequality in ownership relations.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The programme centres on mobilising the people at all times and sees politics as the means of transformation.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Not discussed; Marxist sympathy for ideology critique but nothing in the sources.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: The programme says capitalists use state power, law and administration to protect profit, not mainly culture, so this is inferred.

native-born-offices.rationale: Not discussed; the programme's pluralism and equality aims weigh against it.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: PMPD seeks an independent self-reliant national economy yet invites foreign capital and technology, so it rejects relying only on own resources.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Border claims from past wars are not covered in the sources I read, so no stated position exists for the programme.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Not discussed; the programme's equal-rights and pluralism stance weighs against ethnic political leadership.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Not discussed; Marxist-Leninists would likely sympathise, but nothing in sources states it.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: The sources criticise one-party communist rule but do not equate fascism and communism, so the claim is inferred as disfavoured.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: The causes of the American Civil War are outside the sources I read; the claim is inferred to be rejected from a Marxist reading of history.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Not discussed; no principle of PMPD decides it.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Not discussed; no source takes a line on this.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Not discussed; no source takes a line on this.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: The programme stresses a Nepal-specific path but calls multiparty methods transferable to all democratic societies, so adherents are split.

paid-care-work.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from women's equality commitments.

filial-duty.rationale: Filial obligations are a family-ethics question absent from the sources; nothing in PMPD addresses it.

office-by-exam.rationale: Not discussed; leaders are to be chosen through election and competition.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: The programme welcomes foreign capital under constitutional protection, though strategic sectors are not discussed.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from women's equality commitments.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Leaders are to be periodically approved by the people, but binding mandates and instant recall are not mentioned.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: The party backs a welfare system guaranteeing social security, which is inconsistent with privatised pension accounts; inferred.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Land reform leaves farmers using and owning land, not holding it as community property.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Inferred from parliamentary government with rule of law and separated powers.

single-official-language.rationale: Bhandari cited linguistic diversity as a basis for pluralism, which weighs against a sole official language.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from national independence emphasis despite openness to foreign capital.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Legal tests for discrimination are not discussed; the programme opposes discrimination but sets no doctrine on intent.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from criticism of profit-driven accumulation.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Panchsheel foreign policy includes non-interference, so arming insurgents abroad is rejected.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Panchsheel includes respect for sovereignty and non-interference, which excludes invading an ally to keep it in a bloc.

corporate-influence.rationale: The programme says capitalists use state power, law and administration for profit, which fits worry about corporate influence.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Not discussed; sovereignty concerns and open-society commitments pull in opposite directions.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Birth-rate policy is absent from the sources I read, and PMPD's principles give no direction.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local limits on property purchases are not discussed in the sources; no PMPD principle settles it.

job-guarantee.rationale: Inferred from the party's welfare and social-justice aims and the worker-centred line.

democratic-peace.rationale: Not discussed; PMPD promotes democracy but says nothing on its effects on war.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The programme stresses rule of law and constitutional supremacy, so a blanket denial of any duty to obey is rejected.

non-intervention.rationale: Panchsheel, the stated basis of PMPD foreign policy, includes mutual non-interference.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is not discussed in any source.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Contradicts the programme's pluralism and equal-rights stance; inferred.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Not discussed; no stated PMPD stance, and the programme is not radical on family forms.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The programme upholds the right to seek, receive and impart information and requires an open society.

local-production.rationale: Not discussed; self-reliance suggests partial sympathy, but PMPD also invites foreign capital.

informal-organisation.rationale: The programme builds disciplined parties with democratic centralism and mass mobilisation, not small informal groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The ranking of national against international law is not discussed, and Panchsheel sovereignty pulls against rights commitments.

religious-nation.rationale: Bhandari emphasised Nepal's plural, multi-religious character; a religious definition of nationhood is rejected.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Panchsheel assumes equality among states, so ritual submission and tribute are inconsistent with it.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: The party lists federalism, but revenue-sharing is not discussed.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Inferred from classical Marxist distinction between personal property and means of production; the programme does not discuss it.

defeat-communism.rationale: PMPD is a communist line, so defeating communism rather than coexisting is the opposite of its stance.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Inferred from the mixed-economy model; no source discusses public service delivery.

religion-illusion.rationale: The programme is rooted in dialectical materialism but does not state a view on religion, so adherents are plausibly split.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: The line aims to develop productive forces and national capital as the basis for moving toward socialism, accepting capitalism's material role.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred from the programme's view that ownership relations are the root of discrimination.

socialized-care.rationale: Public provision of housework and childcare is not discussed; the programme's welfare aims give only weak guidance, so it is neutral.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Not discussed; linguistic plurality weighs against purism.

treaties-binding.rationale: Treaties between governments and nations within them are not addressed in the sources I read.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Not discussed; the programme works through parliament and a mixed economy, not self-governing communes.

majority-settlement.rationale: Contradicts pluralism and equality for ethnic groups; inferred.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The programme's goal is socialism and communism, so a third course is rejected.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Historical or religious claims to land are not discussed; the programme's materialism gives no stated line.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Not discussed; included as a factual matter, adherents would be expected to reject.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The programme requires multi-party competition with a strong opposition and says no party or class may be excluded.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Contradicts the freedom of opinion and open society the programme upholds.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Anti-imperialism is central; exploitative colonial governance is rejected.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Not discussed; an Islamic doctrinal claim outside the programme.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: The programme makes people, not religion, the source of legitimacy, so removal by force on religious grounds is rejected.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The programme calls for democratisation of the party, society and state and for people's decisive role.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the concern with discrimination and class.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; inferred from rights commitments.

assisted-dying.rationale: Assisted dying is a medical-ethics question outside the sources; PMPD says nothing on it.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Marxist-Leninist theory in the programme divides left and right fronts, so the division is not obsolete.

alienated-labor.rationale: Marxist theory; inferred from the stress on exploitation, but alienation is not discussed.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Contradicts pluralism and equal rights; inferred.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The programme says people are the source of state power since they overthrew belief in supernatural sources.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Religious dress rules in state institutions are not discussed; open-society and secular leanings point in different directions.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from women's rights commitments.

social-market-economy.rationale: The programme combines a mixed economy and welfare aims with competition and rule of law, not laissez-faire or full state control.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Not discussed; Panchsheel favours peace but the party works within a state with an army.

rich-first.rationale: Inferred from egalitarian aims; the programme does not endorse letting some get rich first.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Panchsheel foreign policy suggests non-alignment between great-power blocs.

dynastic-succession.rationale: The party helped end the monarchy and requires leaders to win periodic election approval.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Mutual credit banking is not discussed in the sources; no PMPD principle bears on it.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Anti-imperialism suggests resistance to lender conditions, but nothing is stated.

property-franchise.rationale: The programme specifies periodic elections on universal adult franchise.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Not discussed; ecofeminist theory is outside the sources.

reification.rationale: Marxist theory but not discussed in the sources; inferred.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Inferred from class analysis of capitalists' use of state power; the programme itself defends free speech under pluralism.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The programme requires that anyone can be punished only by a formal decision of an authorised legal body and that those in power not decide arbitrarily.

racial-franchise.rationale: The programme specifies universal adult franchise and ends discrimination, so franchise on ethnic lines is excluded.

online-participation.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the open-society and participation emphasis.

open-government-data.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from open society and transparency.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Not discussed; the programme relies on elections and parties.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Reinterpreting religious doctrine is a question internal to religions and absent from the sources.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The programme says unlimited accumulation of wealth leads to discrimination and exploitation and that capitalists use state power.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from equality commitments.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The programme upholds an open, plural society, so state promotion of atheism in schools is not endorsed.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Not discussed; the programme requires a state and legal bodies, so abolition is rejected.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The programme sets majority government with minority opposition, not guaranteed executive power-sharing.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The party backs a welfare system guaranteeing social security through the state.

vote-delegation.rationale: Not discussed; the programme relies on representative parties and periodic elections.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Extinction risk is not discussed anywhere in the sources, so there is no stated position.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from equality commitments.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from women's equality commitments.

rent-control.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from tilt toward the poor.

abolish-ip.rationale: Patents and copyright are not discussed in the sources I read, so the answer is neutral.

uniformed-youth.rationale: The programme rejects militarised party forms and stresses open pluralist society.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Inferred from Panchsheel peaceful foreign policy and non-alignment.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred from Panchsheel's respect for sovereignty and non-alignment.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from human-rights commitments.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The programme says ownership of resources is the root of discrimination and exploitation, favouring rewarding work.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: The programme says violence is not to be met with peace and endorses force against violent suppression.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Not discussed; Marxist historical analysis stresses changing class relations, not unbroken national identity.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Not discussed; feminist theory is not in the sources.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: The idea of a diaspora homeland as cultural centre is not discussed in the sources.

culture-before-state.rationale: Not discussed; the programme focuses on state power and revolution.

god-not-male.rationale: Gendered language about God is a religious-studies question absent from the sources.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Feminist scriptural criticism is outside the sources; PMPD gives no line on religious texts.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: The programme builds a pluralist, equal-rights state and rejects ethnic ownership.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Merging administrative regions by ethnicity is not discussed, although the party lists federalism among its principles.

independent-unions.rationale: The programme says people's rights must not be controlled by party or state; union independence is inferred.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The programme says the proletarian working class should maintain leadership and control in the state through initiative and competition.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Inferred from the mixed economy with state-led social infrastructure.

second-chamber.rationale: Not discussed; Nepal's parliament has two houses and the party works within it.

municipal-property.rationale: The programme does not hold with ownership by local communities, aiming at socialism under a national state.

confederal-coordination.rationale: The programme builds a parliamentary state, not confederal assemblies.

family-wage.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from socialist support for fair wages.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Drug regulation is not discussed in any source; neutral by lack of stated position.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Research funding on ageing is absent from the sources I read, so no stated position exists.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Not discussed; rule-of-law and state tilt suggest disfavour.

online-anonymity.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from free expression emphasis.

person-over-state.rationale: The programme says people's rights must not be controlled by party or state and fundamental rights not confiscated.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The programme speaks of developing the country materially and spiritually, but is materialist in philosophy.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: The party lists federalism, which implies constitutionally protected regional powers.

gm-crops.rationale: Genetic engineering in agriculture is not discussed in the sources; PMPD gives no direction.

dense-cities.rationale: Urban form and its environmental effects are not discussed in the sources, so this is neutral.

racial-pride.rationale: Not discussed; class-based analysis weighs against it.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Panchsheel includes non-aggression, so force only in defence fits.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: The party's accounts cite foreign interventionist forces in Nepal's instability, but partition plots are not mentioned.

free-public-college.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from state provision aims.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Environmental taxation is not discussed in the sources I read.

future-generations.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the concern for developing society.

women-distinct-values.rationale: The sources call for women's proportional representation but say nothing on distinct female values in politics.

arms-reduction.rationale: Inferred from Panchsheel and peaceful coexistence.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from openness stance.

capital-controls.rationale: The programme invites foreign capital and technology under national law, so tight controls are not favoured.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Inferred: the programme works through a constitutional state with separation of powers and elections, which implies state forces alone bear arms.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Inferred: the programme backs Panchsheel peaceful coexistence but is a state-building Marxist-Leninist platform, not one urging soldiers to refuse orders.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Inferred: a Marxist-Leninist party with a welfare and social justice platform would support union bargaining; the sources do not mention it.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: The programme analyses Nepal as semi-colonial and seeks foreign capital on Nepal's terms, which implies changing unequal external economic relations.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Inferred: the sources do not address valuing ecosystems.

sacred-nation.rationale: The party's nationalism is described as left-wing and civic, which suggests the nation is a political community, not a sacred one; inferred.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Inferred: a party with a welfare and social justice platform would favour relief, but the sources do not mention it.

internal-colonialism.rationale: The party backs federalism and a class analysis of exploitation, so regional exploitation is a plausible but unstated fit.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Pyakurel's abstract treats human rights as integral to the programme, which suggests shared dignity; human nature itself is not discussed.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred: the programme stresses pluralism, rights and free competition between parties, which fits independent public media.

religions-one-truth.rationale: The programme includes religious freedom but takes no stand on religious truth; a Marxist party leaves the question aside.

farm-price-support.rationale: The programme aims to modernize agriculture and abolish semi-feudal relations through land reform and a mixed economy; state support for farmers is inferred, not quoted.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Nepal has no nuclear weapons and the programme stresses Panchsheel and peaceful coexistence; a nuclear deterrent is not part of it.

workers-own-party.rationale: The programme is the platform of a communist party that claims to represent workers and peasants in competitive multiparty elections.

ban-fgm.rationale: The programme commits to human rights and a socialist party would support banning harmful practices; no source discusses FGM.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: The programme commits to human rights, equality and social justice, and Nepali communist parties backed women's property rights; the sources do not mention inheritance directly.

one-language-many-names.rationale: The programme does not address language naming; inferred as indifferent.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: A socialist mixed economy with state regulation is favored over litigation as the main tool; inferred.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Nepal's communists stand for elected representation and abolishing feudal privilege; official roles for customary chiefs are not part of it.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: The programme prioritizes production growth and rights equally and does not rank the environment over liberty; sources are silent.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Not addressed by the programme; inferred as neutral.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: The programme does not address immigration, and Nepal's communists back multilingual rights; inferred as neutral.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Inferred from the programme's identification of workers as the decisive class and its Marxist labour orientation; closed-shop rules suit union strength.

voter-id.rationale: Not discussed; the programme commits to free elections but the sources say nothing on voter identification.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred from the programme's commitment to human rights and a secular democratic state with freedom of religion.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The programme's Marxist foundation of democracy treats it as real popular rule and social justice, not only competitive elections.

premarital-sex.rationale: Not discussed; a Marxist-Leninist party in a socially conservative Nepali society, with no stated position.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred from the programme's commitment to human rights and civil liberties.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Inferred from the programme's welfare system guaranteeing social security for all and a mixed economy rather than a single cash payment.

women-suffrage.rationale: The programme commits to universal human rights and equal citizenship within multiparty elections.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Inferred: Marxist analysis blames class and feudal structures, but the sources do not single out religion.

race-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from the Marxist view that class and social relations, not nature, shape social groups.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred from the party's social-justice and equality commitments; the sources do not mention gender agencies.
